acceptanceCriteria: dogfood-check reports linked/unlinked over the requirement IDs the bound change cites or traces, with a test that a lane adding N traced requirements reports linked=N; or the OCM coverage members are removed from the SUMMARY and the OCM spec is amended in the same change.
body:
Observed on every lane this week (PR #855: `dogfood-check: SUMMARY cem=accepted hunks=4 supported=4 ... ocm=ready-for-review requirements=56 linked=0 unlinked=56` then `dogfood-check: PASS`). Each lane adds requirements and tests that trace them (REQUIREMENTS.tsv rows, test names per ID), yet the OCM line reports zero linked requirements for the whole intent spec and the check passes regardless.

Expected: either the linker counts the requirement IDs that the change's citations and traceability rows actually reference (so a lane that adds CEM-V1-226..229 shows linked=4 of the IDs it touched, not 0 of 56), or the line is removed from the SUMMARY and the spec stops describing it as coverage. A number that is always zero and never gates is noise that trains readers to ignore the summary.
Actual: linked=0 on passing lanes; nothing consumes the value.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: dogfood-check: `requirements=56 linked=0 unlinked=56` still passes; the OCM intent coverage line carries no signal
